html:
The Battle of Trafalgar was fought on 21 October 1805 off Cape Trafalgar, on the southwest coast of Spain. A British fleet of 27 ships under Admiral Horatio Nelson beat a combined French and Spanish fleet of 33 under Admiral Villeneuve.

Napoleon had planned to invade Britain, and for that he needed to control the English Channel. His fleets failed to gather, and in August he marched his army away against Austria. Villeneuve, shut in the port of Cádiz, was ordered into the Mediterranean and sailed out. Instead of forming the usual line beside the enemy, Nelson sent his ships in two columns straight at it and cut it into pieces. In the close fighting, faster British gunnery decided the day. The allies lost about 20 ships, the British none. Nelson was shot by a French marksman on his flagship, HMS Victory. He died three hours later, knowing he had won.

The battle gave the Royal Navy command of the seas for a century. Unable to invade Britain, Napoleon tried to ruin its trade with a blockade of Europe. Enforcing it drew him into Spain and Russia, and so to his fall in the Napoleonic Wars.
